journey.title: Treatment chemicals award 2027 to 2029, for the Procurement Committee
journey.prompt: Helena needs the treatment chemicals award for the Procurement Committee on Thursday 12 November, with the paper by 5 November. Work out what we buy across Water, Hazardous Waste and Energy and what it costs today, compare the bids in SE-2026-031 on landed cost, show how many days of cover each plant holds under the Corrigan force majeure, and draft the award paper, the award schedule in the 2024 structure and a few slides for the committee. Attached: the bid comparison export and the 2024 award schedule.

questions.title: Corrigan is in force majeure on ferric chloride: how should its bid count?
questions.text: Corrigan's L2 bid is the lowest at $415.00 a ton landed, but it has shipped 60% of contract volume since 12 October and cannot confirm when full supply returns. The policy lets a supplier without continuity be capped or kept as secondary.

tiles.t: Secondary at 30%, only once the force majeure lifts

tiles.s: Sabine Coast alone; $0.22M a year less saving

questions.title: Which volumes should the award rest on?
questions.text: The 2027 dosing plans add Ashby Water Treatment Works and come to 102,280 tons a year; the FY26 run rate is 96,730. Energy's plans, 10% of the volume, are the November 2025 vintage.

tiles.t: The 2027 dosing plans, Energy marked provisional
The plans, with the run rate beside them

nodes.title: State what the group buys and what it costs today
nodes.purpose: The seven chemicals by business, the 2027 volumes and today's landed cost.
nodes.how: Volumes from the 2027 dosing plans by business and site; 2026 contract prices plus freight from the rate card; what was ordered to September as the check.
nodes.check: Volumes sum to the dosing plans; spend to September reconciles to the order lines.

nodes.title: Check supply today: cover at each plant and the Corrigan allocation
nodes.purpose: How exposed each plant is while Corrigan ships 60%.
nodes.how: Days of cover per plant and chemical against the minimum; Corrigan's order lines since 12 October; the spot lines under FMX and their premium. The allocation is quoted as Corrigan's statement, never counted as supply.
nodes.check: Cover counts only what is in the tanks.

nodes.title: Compare the bids on landed cost
nodes.purpose: For each lot, the lowest qualified landed cost and what it saves.
nodes.how: Price plus average freight for every bid, against today's landed cost, on the volumes agreed; unqualified bidders shown and not awarded.
nodes.check: Every lot's saving recomputes from volume, today's landed cost and the awarded landed cost.

nodes.title: Check qualification and continuity of each awarded bidder
nodes.purpose: Whether every bidder the award names can be awarded and can keep supplying.
nodes.how: For each awarded bidder: qualification for the lot, stated capacity against the volume, delivery record, any corrective action, and the vendor record the contract will sit on.
nodes.check: Every awarded bidder is qualified and can carry its volume, or the gap is named.

nodes.title: Three ways to award
nodes.purpose: One award to put to the committee, with what it trades off.
nodes.how: Weigh the award by lot on landed cost against awarding as bid with Corrigan primary, or extending today's agreements and re-bidding ferric; state each trade-off and every caveat that reached it.
nodes.check: The recommendation names its remaining caveats and the alternatives it rejected.

nodes.title: Build the deliverables you chose
nodes.purpose: What you agreed while planning, built on the recommendation chosen: for Helena by 5 November.
nodes.how: The award paper on the committee template; the award schedule in the 2024 structure; a short deck with the award on its own slides. Every figure linked to the step that produced it.
nodes.check: Every figure links back to its step.
